section: A. Architectural alternatives and the contracts they actually provide
title: Minimal cross-mode contract
requested_scope: Specify what batch and live modes must agree on: source subject, obligations, imported environment, assumptions, and accepted claims. Construct cases where diagnostics, proof terms, or timings differ legitimately. Determine which equivalence is necessary without requiring byte-identical incidental artifacts.
specific_remaining_delta: A full same-subject batch/live equivalence contract across obligations, imports, assumptions, and acceptable diagnostic differences.

section: A. Architectural alternatives and the contracts they actually provide
title: Shared compiler core versus separate analysis engine
requested_scope: Compare pinned Lean, TypeScript, Roslyn, clangd, and rust-analyzer boundaries, including where editor approximations diverge from compilation. Identify which APIs genuinely share semantics and which require a fresh compiler oracle; assess what each precedent supports for Anneal.
specific_remaining_delta: A pinned comparison of TypeScript, Roslyn, clangd, and rust-analyzer APIs against Lean plus a compiler-oracle rule for Anneal.

section: A. Architectural alternatives and the contracts they actually provide
title: Embedded-language precedents
requested_scope: Examine representative Razor, Volar, or similar projection systems for virtual document identity, generated spans, completion edits, and multiple language servers. Reproduce a small ambiguous mapping or cross-language edit. Separate reusable mechanisms from assumptions that fail for proof contexts or compiled imports.
specific_remaining_delta: A reproduced Razor/Volar-like ambiguous virtual-document mapping or cross-language edit under exact source pins.

section: A. Architectural alternatives and the contracts they actually provide
title: One-shot, per-project, and shared-service topologies
requested_scope: Compare a fresh process per operation, persistent project workers, and an optional shared broker on identical fixtures. Measure isolation, startup, reconstruction, and coordination costs. Determine when the simplest one-shot design is adequate and what a daemon would actually save.
specific_remaining_delta: Matched one-shot, per-project worker, and shared-broker workload with startup, isolation, reconstruction, and cost measurements.

section: A. Architectural alternatives and the contracts they actually provide
title: Snapshot engine versus a versioned job scheduler
requested_scope: Implement minimal competing orchestration models with fake backends before choosing an incremental database. Replay identical edits, cancellations, and dependency changes. Identify the smallest model that prevents mixed or stale acceptance, and the workload that would justify a richer engine.
specific_remaining_delta: Matched minimal scheduler/database alternatives under dependency changes and cancellations; the fake-stage and finite models cover only selected schedules.

section: A. Architectural alternatives and the contracts they actually provide
title: Stage API and error boundaries
requested_scope: Prototype structured requests/results for Charon, Aeneas, and Lean, separating semantic inputs from CLI output, process policy, and artifact storage. Inject failures, progress events, and stdout/stderr contamination. Test whether batch and live adapters can use the same contract without backend-specific state leaking upward.
specific_remaining_delta: A structured Charon/Aeneas/Lean adapter contract with injected progress, stdout/stderr contamination, and shared batch/live use.

section: A. Architectural alternatives and the contracts they actually provide
title: Cancellation, reuse, and ownership contracts
requested_scope: Specify separately who owns work, who can cancel it, who can consume its result, and when cached work may be reused. Model two clients sharing a job. Look for cases where cancelling one request incorrectly kills another or permits an obsolete result to publish.
specific_remaining_delta: A shared in-flight real backend with per-consumer cancellation and cache reuse ownership, beyond symbolic/fake stages.

section: A. Architectural alternatives and the contracts they actually provide
title: Minimal upstream changes
requested_scope: Identify missing observable identities, reset operations, overlay hooks, and source spans at exact upstream pins. Compare adapters with small upstream API proposals and coarse fallback behavior. Distinguish requirements for correctness from optional latency improvements; preserve a viable path without upstream changes where one exists.
specific_remaining_delta: Exact pinned upstream API gap inventory plus adapter and small upstream-patch comparison.

section: B. Workspace snapshots, document ownership, and coherent inputs
title: Input closure of one verification subject
requested_scope: Enumerate actual source, manifest, lockfile, feature, target, environment, generated-file, model, and toolchain inputs. Perturb each while holding filenames fixed. Identify omitted dependencies that change extracted code, obligations, or proof interpretation and distinguish declared inputs from untracked external effects.
specific_remaining_delta: A complete compilation/verification input tuple with dependency, cfg, target, build-script, environment, model, and tool perturbations.

section: B. Workspace snapshots, document ownership, and coherent inputs
title: Capturing a coherent live filesystem
requested_scope: Compare immutable materialization with read-and-revalidate capture while files change. Include renames, symlinks, generated outputs, and large trees. Preserve a witness of which bytes were read; test whether validation can accept a mixed snapshot and what assumptions prevent that.
specific_remaining_delta: Large-tree capture with rename/symlink/output mutation and a coherent witness under actual concurrent edits.

section: B. Workspace snapshots, document ownership, and coherent inputs
title: Clocks, generations, and ABA changes
requested_scope: Distinguish document versions, workspace revisions, model generations, and process epochs. Exercise content A→B→A, close/reopen with reset versions, workspace recreation, and reused request IDs. Determine which identities prevent an old result from masquerading as a current one without needlessly disabling content-based reuse.
specific_remaining_delta: Reused request IDs, closed/reopened version reset, workspace recreation, and A→B→A against a real engine.

section: B. Workspace snapshots, document ownership, and coherent inputs
title: Disk versus open-buffer ownership
requested_scope: Exercise open, change, save, external overwrite, close, rename, delete, and reopen. Determine when disk or client text is authoritative and how conflicts surface. Include a buffer that remains open after its file disappears; avoid silently replacing unsaved text with a disk reread.
specific_remaining_delta: Full editor buffer lifecycle including save, external overwrite, rename, deletion, and reopened authority transfer.

section: B. Workspace snapshots, document ownership, and coherent inputs
title: Coherent multi-document changes
requested_scope: Change a proof and its helper, or two Rust modules, as one logical operation while queries run. Compare atomic workspace edits with ordered individual updates. Establish whether intermediate states are queryable, provisional, or rejected, and how a batch invocation selects the same intended snapshot.
specific_remaining_delta: A proof/helper or two-module atomic workspace edit under in-flight queries and explicit provisional-state semantics.

section: B. Workspace snapshots, document ownership, and coherent inputs
title: Multiple writers to one workspace
requested_scope: Race an editor, MCP agent, generator, and external filesystem tool. Compare exclusive document ownership, compare-and-swap edits, and explicit forks. Test conflict detection and lost-update prevention without assuming that all clients share one transport or obey one editor's version counter.
specific_remaining_delta: Four actual writers sharing one workspace, including lost-update and fork/exclusive-owner controls.

section: B. Workspace snapshots, document ownership, and coherent inputs
title: Subset freshness and conservative invalidation
requested_scope: Change unrelated files while a proof query runs. Compare global-revision rejection with dependency-scoped acceptance, including dependencies discovered during processing. Determine whether narrower freshness checks are sound and useful; retain coarse invalidation as the baseline rather than assuming finer reuse is necessary.
specific_remaining_delta: Dependency-scoped versus global freshness on unrelated and newly discovered dependencies with measured reuse.

section: B. Workspace snapshots, document ownership, and coherent inputs
title: Reconstruction after Anneal restart
requested_scope: Recreate a workspace from disk, a retained snapshot, or reconnected client buffers after losing all orchestration memory. Verify subject identity, unsaved edits, imports, and outstanding-result classification. Determine the minimum retained state and what must instead expire or require the client to resend text.
specific_remaining_delta: Anneal restart reconstruction from disk, retained snapshot, and reconnecting unsaved buffers.

section: C. Locating Lean annotations and attaching them to Rust subjects
title: Tolerant annotation discovery during typing
requested_scope: Compare candidate comment, attribute, or delimited encodings under incomplete Rust, unfinished Lean, missing delimiters, and temporarily malformed nesting. Determine which regions can still be located safely without compiling Rust, and when the editor must preserve text but suspend semantic attachment.
specific_remaining_delta: Real candidate annotation encodings and tolerant parser recovery under unfinished Rust and Lean.

section: C. Locating Lean annotations and attaching them to Rust subjects
title: A justified proof-only edit classifier
requested_scope: Test edits to purported Lean-only regions with macros that inspect attributes/comments, source inclusion, and build-time readers. Determine the assumptions under which Rust semantics and extraction inputs really remain unchanged. Record unknown cases that require re-extraction rather than declaring every comment edit harmless.
specific_remaining_delta: A full proof-only classifier challenged by macro, include, and build-time readers in actual extraction inputs.

section: C. Locating Lean annotations and attaching them to Rust subjects
title: Compiler-backed annotation attachment
requested_scope: Exercise conditional compilation, expanded and generated items, aliases, trait defaults, local items, and repeated names. Relate the authored annotation to the actual extracted declaration. Require explicit ambiguity or missing-subject outcomes when a source-level locator cannot establish that correspondence.
specific_remaining_delta: Compiler-backed annotation attachment across cfg, aliases, trait defaults, local/generated items, and explicit ambiguity outcomes.

section: C. Locating Lean annotations and attaching them to Rust subjects
title: One source file, several compilation subjects
requested_scope: Open a file shared by library, tests, binaries, feature sets, or target triples whose generated models differ. Determine how a proof query selects its subject and how mismatches are exposed. Test whether stable annotation identity can remain separate from subject-specific proof context.
specific_remaining_delta: Subject selection across the same source in lib/test/bin, features, and target triples with model/proof mismatch signaling.

section: C. Locating Lean annotations and attaching them to Rust subjects
title: Annotation identity across structural edits
requested_scope: Move, duplicate, split, reorder, and delete annotated items while requests are outstanding. Compare range-, syntax-, compiler-, and explicit-ID-based identity schemes. Detect erroneous reassignment of a completed proof to a different obligation; preserve deliberate duplication without assuming names or offsets are globally unique.
specific_remaining_delta: Annotation identity across move, duplicate, split, reorder, and deletion while results remain in flight.

section: C. Locating Lean annotations and attaching them to Rust subjects
title: Multiple annotations and shared helpers
requested_scope: Test declarations, specifications, proofs, imports, namespace commands, and helper lemmas distributed across annotations. Examine ordering, visibility, name collisions, and recursive dependencies. Determine which layouts preserve the authored meaning and which create unwanted dependencies between otherwise independent proofs.
specific_remaining_delta: Multiple annotations and helper/import ordering with visibility, collision, and recursion controls.

section: C. Locating Lean annotations and attaching them to Rust subjects
title: Editing against an unavailable or broken Rust model
requested_scope: Introduce a Rust syntax error, unsupported extraction, or changed function signature while continuing a Lean proof. Compare stopping interaction with explicitly using the last prepared model. Test whether users and agents understand the model's age and avoid treating provisional feedback as current verification.
specific_remaining_delta: Continued proof interaction against an explicitly named last-good model through Rust syntax, extraction, and signature failures.

section: C. Locating Lean annotations and attaching them to Rust subjects
title: Preserving authored source through regeneration
requested_scope: Regenerate after Rust edits while Lean annotations contain unsaved changes, custom formatting, and unsupported-but-preserved text. Confirm that canonical user text is not reconstructed from LLBC or generated Lean. Test ownership rules for external proof/model files and explicit overrides without choosing a mandatory storage layout.
specific_remaining_delta: Preservation of unsaved authored Lean, formatting, and unsupported text through regeneration and external edits.

section: D. Exact projections, provenance, and safe round-trip edits
title: Coordinate conversion property suite
requested_scope: Generate source containing supplementary characters, combining marks, tabs, CRLF, empty lines, and boundary positions. Round-trip byte, scalar, and negotiated LSP coordinates where invertible. Treat lossy display-width coordinates and invalid boundaries explicitly; retain original bytes rather than silently normalizing Unicode.
specific_remaining_delta: Negotiated LSP encoding round trips in a real host/projection pipeline; property fixture covers scalar/UTF-16 boundaries only.

section: D. Exact projections, provenance, and safe round-trip edits
title: Piecewise projection invertibility
requested_scope: Test stripping prefixes/indentation, escaping delimiters, and inserting scaffolding. Establish which Lean ranges map exactly to authored Rust ranges, including zero-width insertions. Reject edits crossing synthetic gaps or multiple source segments unless a deliberate transformation can preserve the surrounding source.
specific_remaining_delta: Actual Anneal annotation stripping, escaping, and scaffolding with exact source-map inversion and cross-segment rejection.

section: D. Exact projections, provenance, and safe round-trip edits
title: One-to-many and many-to-one provenance
requested_scope: Generate several obligations from one annotation and combine several annotations in one Lean declaration. Test query routing, related diagnostics, and edit ambiguity. Distinguish selecting a proof context from choosing an editable origin; an attribution anchor must not authorize replacement of unrelated Rust text.
specific_remaining_delta: Real one-to-many obligations and many-to-one declarations with routing, related diagnostics, and edit ambiguity.

section: D. Exact projections, provenance, and safe round-trip edits
title: One generator for batch and live text
requested_scope: Materialize and stream the same projection through separate sinks, including incomplete proofs and changed imports. Compare text, module context, source maps, and elaborated declarations. Detect accidental differences from newline handling, temporary filenames, omitted scaffolding, or a second editor-only code path.
specific_remaining_delta: One generator streaming and materializing identical context, maps, and declarations under incomplete proofs/import changes.

section: D. Exact projections, provenance, and safe round-trip edits
title: Revision-safe projected patches
requested_scope: Obtain a Lean edit, then change the Rust document before applying it. Check both expected source bytes and projection identity, including edits elsewhere that shift ranges. Test atomic application and conflict reporting; a plausible re-mapped position must not silently overwrite a different proof.
specific_remaining_delta: Real projected edits with source-and-projection CAS after unrelated shifting edits and atomic conflict reporting.

section: D. Exact projections, provenance, and safe round-trip edits
title: Completion and code-action edits beyond the cursor
requested_scope: Exercise snippets, additional text edits, new imports, qualified-name fixes, and edits spanning generated/user regions. Determine which operations can be projected back safely and which need a specialized Anneal action. Preserve snippet placeholders and reject unsupported transformations rather than partially applying them.
specific_remaining_delta: Completion snippets, additional edits/imports, code actions, and synthetic-region crossings in real projection.

section: D. Exact projections, provenance, and safe round-trip edits
title: Diagnostics and provenance fidelity
requested_scope: Produce errors in copied proof text, generated scaffolding, generated models, and external imports. Preserve the original Lean location plus the exact or approximate Rust explanation. Test range quality, related information, absent source, and responsibility selection without making a synthetic error look user-authored.
specific_remaining_delta: Full diagnostic source ownership across generated scaffolding, model, external imports, and ambiguous/absent spans.

section: D. Exact projections, provenance, and safe round-trip edits
title: Mapping stability and cost during edit streams
requested_scope: Fuzz insertion/deletion around annotation boundaries and measure full versus incremental projection updates. Validate maps against regenerated ground truth after every edit. Determine whether incremental mapping complexity earns enough latency improvement to justify its additional invalidation and correctness burden.
specific_remaining_delta: Boundary-edit fuzz on actual annotation grammar plus measured full versus incremental mapping latency.

section: E. Projected Lean documents and module layout
title: Virtual URI and file-backed document compatibility
requested_scope: Test custom schemes, file URIs for nonexistent files, untitled buffers, and stable on-disk shells under supported Lean launch modes. Exercise import resolution and `setup-file`. Establish the minimum physical project structure needed for unsaved projected text and ordinary proof queries.
specific_remaining_delta: URI/physical-path behavior across supported Lake launch modes and setup-file with imports, not just direct Lean.

section: E. Projected Lean documents and module layout
title: Stable document identity versus generation paths
requested_scope: Compare stable logical documents with remapped generated imports, generation-specific physical paths, and close/reopen publication. Measure incremental reuse and verify module identity after each transition. Determine whether a stable URI can safely survive environment changes or should deliberately acquire a new worker.
specific_remaining_delta: Existing-worker remapping across generations and measured stable URI versus generation-path reuse.

section: E. Projected Lean documents and module layout
title: Per-annotation, per-file, and per-artifact layouts
requested_scope: Use identical proofs with shared helpers and different model sizes under each layout. Measure worker count, import cost, incremental reuse, and failure isolation. Record semantic restrictions imposed by splitting; fewer files or smaller modules is not automatically the cheaper or more expressive option.
specific_remaining_delta: Per-annotation, per-file, and per-artifact layouts on same proofs with helper visibility and model-size/worker-count costs.

section: E. Projected Lean documents and module layout
title: Prefix reuse under generated-context changes
requested_scope: Change early imports, namespaces, options, generated declarations, and late proof tactics separately. Observe Lean's actual elaboration reuse and cancellation. Identify which generation strategies preserve useful prefixes and which merely keep filenames stable while forcing complete re-elaboration.
specific_remaining_delta: Prefix reuse measurements for early import/namespace/option changes versus late tactics, including cancellation.

section: E. Projected Lean documents and module layout
title: Context fidelity of wrappers and scaffolding
requested_scope: Compare direct Lean with projected annotations under namespaces, sections, variables, local instances, notation, macros, and options. Inspect elaborated proposition and dependencies, not only successful checking. Find wrapper transformations that accidentally capture names or change the statement being proved.
specific_remaining_delta: Elaborated proposition/dependency comparison for projected wrappers under local instances, macros, notation, and options.

section: E. Projected Lean documents and module layout
title: Open documents that import other unsaved documents
requested_scope: Keep both producer and proof open, change only the producer buffer, and compare server behavior with compiled-disk imports. Determine whether simultaneous unsaved cross-module semantics are supported, require materialization, or need explicit restrictions; do not assume all open buffers form one live import environment.
specific_remaining_delta: A supported two-open-document unsaved-import design or explicit staged materialization protocol.

section: E. Projected Lean documents and module layout
title: Dependency cycles and generated declaration order
requested_scope: Construct cross-annotation helper dependencies, generated specifications referencing models, and mutually dependent proof modules. Compare legal grouping and explicit cycle rejection. Determine which graph belongs to generation, compilation, or proof checking and avoid hiding cycles through stale compiled modules.
specific_remaining_delta: Cross-annotation helper graph, model references, legal grouping, and cycle rejection beyond a simple Lake cycle.

section: E. Projected Lean documents and module layout
title: Scratch proof forks preserve full context
requested_scope: Clone a projected document for tactic experiments, varying module identity, options, imports, and surrounding commands. Compare results with applying the candidate to the real proof. Detect experiments that work only because the scratch context or pre-elaborated prefix differs from the intended document.
specific_remaining_delta: Scratch proof forks with matched module identity, options, imports, surrounding commands, and real-candidate replay.

section: F. Lean query causality, tactic state, and worker lifetimes
title: Exact-version goal query protocol
requested_scope: Compare serialized document access, client-side version fences, snapshot-specific documents, and any upstream version-aware operations. Introduce actual concurrent edits before, during, and after readiness waits and goal requests. Determine which protocol can justify the returned version rather than merely label an unversioned response.
specific_remaining_delta: Interleavings before/during/after goal wait on exact versions and a chosen client fence/worker replacement protocol.

section: F. Lean query causality, tactic state, and worker lifetimes
title: Readiness is not a single boolean
requested_scope: Delay parsing, imports, elaboration, asynchronous tasks, diagnostics, and tactic information separately. Test available wait operations and progress notifications. Distinguish ready-at-position, whole-file completion, imports-out-of-date, and permanent failure, including files whose diagnostics are temporarily empty.
specific_remaining_delta: Separate parsing/import/elaboration/async task delays with ready-at-position and whole-file status classification.

section: F. Lean query causality, tactic state, and worker lifetimes
title: Tactic-position selection semantics
requested_scope: Query before/after tactics, within whitespace, at nested goals, tactic combinators, macros, errors, and EOF. Compare plain goals and interactive goals. Preserve exact coordinates and expected selection so an agent knows whether it is seeing input goals, output goals, or no applicable tactic state.
specific_remaining_delta: Position-selection matrix for nested tactics, combinators, macro/error/EOF, and interactive versus plain goals.

section: F. Lean query causality, tactic state, and worker lifetimes
title: Rich RPC object lifetimes
requested_scope: Retain interactive goal/context handles across edits, cancellation, file close, worker restart, and server restart. Test reconnect and expiration handling. Determine which data can be copied into durable results and which must remain explicitly scoped to a live worker/RPC session.
specific_remaining_delta: Interactive RPC handle lifetime across edit, cancel, close, worker/server restart and reconnect.

section: F. Lean query causality, tactic state, and worker lifetimes
title: Worker incarnation and request-ID reuse
requested_scope: Delay responses while replacing a worker and reusing file versions or transport request numbers. Verify that old responses, notifications, and RPC references cannot enter the new context. Test clean shutdown separately from forced termination and a crashed worker restarted by its supervisor.
specific_remaining_delta: Actual worker incarnation replacement with delayed old responses, reused IDs, and clean versus forced termination.

section: F. Lean query causality, tactic state, and worker lifetimes
title: Partial and failed elaboration
requested_scope: Place a valid proof before and after unfinished declarations, unknown tactics, timeouts, and recoverable syntax errors. Query reachable positions and inspect diagnostics. Determine what useful state is available without implying that the full module or its intended obligations have been checked.
specific_remaining_delta: Goal availability before and after partial declarations, unknown tactics, timeouts, and recoverable errors.

section: F. Lean query causality, tactic state, and worker lifetimes
title: Historical queries versus latest-only queries
requested_scope: Compare rejecting superseded requests, retaining old snapshots, and rebuilding a requested revision in isolation. Measure storage and latency, including rapid edits that continually supersede work. Establish explicit semantics for latest-at-start, latest-at-completion, and exact historical requests rather than silently switching among them.
specific_remaining_delta: Latest-only versus retained historical snapshots with measured storage/latency during rapid edits.

section: F. Lean query causality, tactic state, and worker lifetimes
title: Imported-environment attestation
requested_scope: Determine what a worker can report about loaded module artifacts, options, plugins, and build identities. Compare explicit instrumentation with a fresh-worker construction whose inputs are controlled. Show how Anneal could establish the actual environment used, not just store an intended generation tag beside the response.
specific_remaining_delta: Worker attestation of loaded artifacts/options/plugins or validated fresh-worker construction at the real project boundary.

section: G. Model generations and imported-environment transitions
title: Refresh matrix across server launch modes
requested_scope: Repeat the imported-definition counterexample under `lake serve`, `lake env lean --server`, and explicitly prepared direct Lean where supported. Compare watcher notifications, reopen, file-worker restart, and whole-server restart. Preserve which reset actually restores agreement with a fresh batch check.
specific_remaining_delta: Matched import-refresh matrix under lake serve, lake env lean --server, and direct prepared Lean.

section: G. Model generations and imported-environment transitions
title: Transitive imports, plugins, and option changes
requested_scope: Change a transitive theorem/model, package configuration, server option, macro extension, or native plugin without editing the open proof. Test invalidation and reload boundaries separately. Determine when refreshing one file is sufficient and when process-global state requires a larger restart.
specific_remaining_delta: Transitive import, package option, macro extension, and native plugin invalidation distinct from direct import deletion.

section: G. Model generations and imported-environment transitions
title: Complete-generation publication
requested_scope: Regenerate several interdependent Lean modules and compiled artifact families while readers run. Pause after each write. Compare immutable generation directories, staged publication, and coordinated in-place replacement. Require readers to use a complete old or new generation, never a mixture presented as current.
specific_remaining_delta: Actual multi-module generation/artifact-family staged publication with readers paused after each write.

section: G. Model generations and imported-environment transitions
title: Preparation at permanent paths
requested_scope: Compare building at a final unpublished location with building elsewhere and relocating at publication. Include manifests, traces, module setup, native search paths, and retained workers. Identify every location-bearing input; atomic rename alone must not be treated as proof that prepared state remains valid.
specific_remaining_delta: Prepare at final versus moved path across manifests, traces, setup, native libraries, and retained workers.

section: G. Model generations and imported-environment transitions
title: Obsolete generation completing late
requested_scope: Start generation A, supersede it with B, then let A finish after B publishes. Exercise generated sources, compiled artifacts, diagnostics, and cache insertion independently. Establish where obsolete output may be retained for reuse and where it must be barred from current workspace state.
specific_remaining_delta: Late obsolete real backend output tested independently for generated source, compiled artifacts, diagnostics, and cache insertion.

section: G. Model generations and imported-environment transitions
title: Failed generation and explicit fallback
requested_scope: Fail extraction, translation, compilation, or server preparation after a previous successful generation. Test rollback and continued interaction against the old environment. Require visible model identity and failure status; last-known-good proof feedback must not silently become a current verification result.
specific_remaining_delta: Failure at every extraction/translation/build/server stage with visible last-good model and explicit rollback policy.

section: G. Model generations and imported-environment transitions
title: Deletions, renames, and output-set shrinkage
requested_scope: Remove a Rust item, generated Lean module, import, or obligation and rebuild. Test that obsolete files/artifacts are absent from the selected generation and cannot satisfy resolution accidentally. Include module names reused for different subjects and skipped outputs after partial translator failure.
specific_remaining_delta: Full output-set shrinkage, reused module names, and proof/obligation deletion in a selected real generation.

section: G. Model generations and imported-environment transitions
title: Proof/model change dependency granularity
requested_scope: Separate proof-body edits, theorem-statement edits, exported helper changes, generated-definition changes, and model/assumption changes. Compare conservative rebuilds with finer dependency tracking. Determine which results can remain valid and which contexts must restart, including changes that leave generated filenames unchanged.
specific_remaining_delta: Proof-body/statement/helper/model ablation and sound incremental reuse boundaries on real Lean imports.

section: H. Editor integration and LSP routing
title: Rust and embedded Lean server coexistence
requested_scope: Prototype editor-extension routing, an LSP proxy, and separate servers where supported. Exercise completion, diagnostics, hover, and cancellation inside and outside annotations. Determine the minimum client integration and ensure ordinary Rust features neither disappear nor act on the wrong embedded language.
specific_remaining_delta: Editor extension, LSP proxy, and separate-server prototypes for both Rust and embedded Lean features.

section: H. Editor integration and LSP routing
title: Diagnostic multiplexing and stale clearing
requested_scope: Merge rustc/Charon/Aeneas/Lean diagnostics under distinct origins and revisions. Exercise push/pull clients, empty updates, renamed files, and superseded runs. Confirm that clearing one producer's diagnostics neither removes another's errors nor leaves an old success/error displayed as current.
specific_remaining_delta: Push/pull diagnostic multiplexing with rustc/Charon/Aeneas/Lean origins and stale clearing across rename.

section: H. Editor integration and LSP routing
title: Hover, navigation, and semantic tokens
requested_scope: Map Lean definitions, references, goal-related spans, and tokens into annotations or read-only generated views. Test navigation into imported models and source unavailable locally. Preserve exact versus approximate origins and prevent generated code from masquerading as editable Rust source.
specific_remaining_delta: Mapped hover, definition/reference navigation, semantic tokens, and unavailable imported-source behavior.

section: H. Editor integration and LSP routing
title: Rename and cross-file workspace edits
requested_scope: Rename Lean helpers used across annotations and external proof files while Rust symbols remain unchanged. Test multi-file preconditions, resource operations, and partial client support. Determine whether routing can preserve atomic intent or must reject a rename whose generated or ambiguous portions cannot be edited safely.
specific_remaining_delta: Cross-file Lean rename/workspace edits with Rust symbols unchanged and partial client capability controls.

section: H. Editor integration and LSP routing
title: Lean InfoView and RPC integration
requested_scope: Test whether the existing InfoView can display goals for projected Rust positions, including RPC sessions, widgets, hyperlinks, and reconnects. Compare extension glue with a minimal Anneal view. Identify capabilities lost through simple text-goal forwarding and distinguish required proof interaction from optional rich UI.
specific_remaining_delta: Actual InfoView widget/RPC/hyperlink flow from a Rust-hosted proof position through reconnect.

section: H. Editor integration and LSP routing
title: Position encodings and client capability negotiation
requested_scope: Exercise supported LSP encodings, full/incremental synchronization, document versions, and feature negotiation across representative clients. Translate coordinates at explicit boundaries. Reject unsupported combinations clearly instead of assuming every client and internal API uses Lean's preferred coordinate representation.
specific_remaining_delta: Representative clients negotiating position encoding, sync modes, versions, and feature fallbacks.

section: H. Editor integration and LSP routing
title: Editor save/build/format interactions
requested_scope: Trigger autosave, format-on-save, file watching, generated-output notifications, and background builds during proof editing. Detect loops, duplicate work, lost edits, and spuriously dirty buffers. Determine which events Anneal should emit and which must remain internal derived-state changes.
specific_remaining_delta: Real editor autosave/format/watch/build events with loop, duplicate-work, and dirty-buffer controls.

section: H. Editor integration and LSP routing
title: Editor disconnect and recovery
requested_scope: Disconnect or restart the editor while Lean and Anneal remain live, then reconnect with differing disk and buffer contents. Test session cleanup, ownership transfer, and result refresh. Determine what can be reconstructed and what must be explicitly resolved before accepting further edits.
specific_remaining_delta: Editor disconnect/reconnect ownership against divergent disk/buffer bytes and live Lean worker.

section: I. MCP state, agent workflows, and shared authority
title: Versioned MCP contract and compatibility
requested_scope: Map the supported MCP revisions and client capabilities to workspace handles, long-running work, cancellation, progress, and result retrieval. Test capability negotiation and fallback. Separate protocol guarantees from implementation conventions and make workspace identity independent of accidental connection reuse.
specific_remaining_delta: Executable MCP revision/capability negotiation and fallback for handles, progress, cancellation, and retrieval.

section: I. MCP state, agent workflows, and shared authority
title: Minimal typed proof-tool surface
requested_scope: Compare source-position queries, annotation/obligation IDs, context retrieval, diagnostics, edits, and verification calls. Include exact snapshot and subject selection in test cases. Measure whether a small tool set suffices without exposing generated filesystem layout or requiring agents to manipulate raw Lean process state.
specific_remaining_delta: A typed minimal proof-tool API exercised on actual subject/snapshot selection and verification.

section: I. MCP state, agent workflows, and shared authority
title: Retry, idempotency, and compare-and-swap semantics
requested_scope: Retry requests after lost responses, including edits, worker creation, and verification starts. Distinguish a replayed request from a new user action. Test deduplication bounds and conflict detection so retries neither duplicate mutations nor silently apply an edit to a later document.
specific_remaining_delta: Lost-response retry of mutations, worker creation, and verification with bounded deduplication and CAS.

section: I. MCP state, agent workflows, and shared authority
title: MCP and editor observe one authority
requested_scope: Attach both clients to the same workspace, including unsaved Rust-hosted Lean. Alternate queries and edits from each and reconnect one client. Verify that the MCP never refreshes authoritative text from disk behind the editor and that both can identify the same projection/model context.
specific_remaining_delta: One actual MCP/editor workspace authority with alternating unsaved edits, queries, and reconnect.

section: I. MCP state, agent workflows, and shared authority
title: Read-only inspection, mutation, and scoped access
requested_scope: Separate permission to query goals, edit authored annotations, alter imports/models, and execute builds. Use controlled local fixtures to test workspace/path scoping and accidental cross-project access. Do not let a generated-code location, resource handle, or model suggestion implicitly authorize a broader write.
specific_remaining_delta: Executed tool access tiers and workspace/path isolation, especially generated-to-authored edit authority.

section: I. MCP state, agent workflows, and shared authority
title: Scratch attempts and candidate application
requested_scope: Try multiple tactics in isolated proof forks, then apply one candidate only after validating its source preconditions. Compare the target proposition, assumptions, and resulting obligations before/after. Detect apparent success obtained by changing the statement, adding admissions, or using a stale scratch environment.
specific_remaining_delta: Isolated scratch tactic attempts applied back under subject/proof CAS and verified against intended context.

section: I. MCP state, agent workflows, and shared authority
title: Cancellation, backpressure, and reconnect over MCP
requested_scope: Interrupt long checks and large result streams over supported transports. Test slow clients, dropped responses, request cancellation, progress loss, and retrieval after reconnection. Determine which work survives and how its result expires without leaking workers or conflating transport failure with proof failure.
specific_remaining_delta: Actual asynchronous MCP progress/result lifecycle with expiry, cancellation, and partial-failure responses.

section: I. MCP state, agent workflows, and shared authority
title: Existing Lean MCP adapters under Anneal conditions
requested_scope: Run representative implementations against unsaved projections, replaced imports, scratch forks, and simultaneous editor access. Identify disk-reread assumptions and process/global caches. Decide which components can be reused unchanged, wrapped, or replaced; tool availability alone does not establish state correctness.
specific_remaining_delta: Two independent MCP clients with concurrent calls, cancellation, and consistent shared workspace observations.

section: J. Cargo, rustc, and Charon input/execution boundaries
title: Saved-Rust baseline versus overlay extraction
requested_scope: Compare saved-only verification, snapshot materialization, and any supported compiler overlay mechanisms. Use identical intended bytes with unsaved annotations and ordinary Rust edits. State precisely which source version each result covers; evaluate whether saved-only Rust preserves useful Lean interaction without misleading users.
specific_remaining_delta: Saved-only versus snapshot-materialized Rust and any compiler overlay on identical intended unsaved bytes, with explicit source-version UX.

section: J. Cargo, rustc, and Charon input/execution boundaries
title: Shadow-workspace fidelity
requested_scope: Materialize workspaces containing path dependencies, `build.rs`, proc macros, `include_*`, environment inputs, and generated files. Compare emitted code and relevant compiler observations with the original location. Detect path-sensitive behavior before assuming a copied tree faithfully represents the same compilation subject.
specific_remaining_delta: Shadow-workspace fidelity for path dependencies, build scripts, proc macros, includes, env, generated files, and path-sensitive compiler output.

section: J. Cargo, rustc, and Charon input/execution boundaries
title: Cargo skipping the Charon-producing invocation
requested_scope: Warm Cargo caches, vary wrappers and target selection, and request extraction repeatedly. Determine when Cargo can report success without producing fresh LLBC. Compare explicit freshness checks and rebuild controls; an old destination file must not serve as evidence that extraction ran.
specific_remaining_delta: Warm-Cargo skipped-Charon controls with wrapper/target variations, fresh LLBC witness, and stale destination rejection.

section: J. Cargo, rustc, and Charon input/execution boundaries
title: Compilation-unit identity and output collisions
requested_scope: Exercise multiple primary targets, host/target units, feature variants, same-named crates, and sibling libraries concurrently. Record actual rustc/Charon invocations and outputs. Verify that each LLBC result corresponds to one intended unit and no invocation-wide destination is overwritten by another producer.
specific_remaining_delta: Concurrent compilation-unit identity for targets, host/target, features, crate-name collisions, and LLBC destination ownership.

section: J. Cargo, rustc, and Charon input/execution boundaries
title: Charon process isolation and reset feasibility
requested_scope: Compare fresh driver processes with any feasible reused library/worker boundary. Run subject A, subject B, then A again after errors and cancellation. Inspect process-global state and compiler lifetimes; reuse is justified only by isolation evidence, not because `charon_lib` can deserialize LLBC.
specific_remaining_delta: Charon A/B/A process/library reset after errors/cancel, compiler lifetime, and isolation evidence.

section: J. Cargo, rustc, and Charon input/execution boundaries
title: Charon output transaction and completeness
requested_scope: Interrupt or fail extraction at multiple stages with a previous successful output present. Test parsing, declared version, subject identity, output completeness, and atomic publication. Distinguish malformed output, partial extraction, unsupported code, and no output rather than relying only on process exit status.
specific_remaining_delta: Interrupted/failing Charon output transaction with schema/version/subject/completeness checks and atomic publication.

section: J. Cargo, rustc, and Charon input/execution boundaries
title: LLBC identity, normalization, and source metadata
requested_scope: Perturb paths, comments, declaration order, tool flags, and compiler revisions. Compare raw LLBC with proposed cache-key normalization. Construct cases where apparently incidental metadata affects annotation association or diagnostics; separate semantic translation reuse from freshness of source provenance.
specific_remaining_delta: LLBC path/comment/order/flag/compiler-revision ablations preserving semantic and source-provenance distinctions.

section: J. Cargo, rustc, and Charon input/execution boundaries
title: Rust-side resource sharing and cleanup
requested_scope: Measure Cargo target directories, compiler incremental data, build-script products, and wrapper processes across parallel snapshot consumers. Compare isolated versus shared writable caches under cancellation. Determine whether eliminating Lake copies merely moves disk amplification or contention into the Rust extraction stage.
specific_remaining_delta: Cargo target/incremental/build-script/wrapper resource sharing under parallel snapshots and cancellation.

section: K. Aeneas translation boundaries and generated output
title: One-shot versus reusable Aeneas worker
requested_scope: Translate A/B/A with differing options, models, and failures through candidate library/daemon boundaries. Compare outputs with fresh processes and inspect global accumulators/configuration. Test cleanup after cancellation; establish a reentrancy contract before measuring a worker pool as a valid optimization.
specific_remaining_delta: Aeneas same-process A/B/A with changed flags/models/failure/cancel, reset evidence, and fresh-process oracle.

section: K. Aeneas translation boundaries and generated output
title: Exact Aeneas request identity
requested_scope: Vary LLBC revision, normalization, translation options, external-model registries, library versions, and naming configuration independently. Determine which inputs affect output or acceptance. Test cache keys against deliberate collisions and distinguish schema compatibility from semantic compatibility.
specific_remaining_delta: Independent LLBC, normalization, options, external registry, library version, and naming input ablations with collision controls.

section: K. Aeneas translation boundaries and generated output
title: Whole-crate versus finer-grained invalidation
requested_scope: Change one function, type, trait implementation, recursive group, or external model and inspect effects elsewhere. Prototype finer reuse only where dependency evidence supports it. Compare with a full translation oracle and retain counterexamples to per-item caching based solely on unchanged item text.
specific_remaining_delta: Changed function/type/trait/recursive group/external model with whole-crate oracle and finer-invalidation counterexamples.

section: K. Aeneas translation boundaries and generated output
title: Generated-name and declaration stability
requested_scope: Apply unrelated edits, helper insertion, reordering, and module moves while keeping a selected Rust behavior unchanged. Measure changes to Lean names, signatures, and proof context. Determine whether stable naming is an upstream opportunity, an adapter concern, or an unavoidable proof-maintenance boundary.
specific_remaining_delta: Generated Lean name/signature/context stability under unrelated edits, helper insertion, reorder, and module moves.

section: K. Aeneas translation boundaries and generated output
title: Multi-file emission and ownership
requested_scope: Exercise generated files, user-maintained external models, output deletion, and partial translation failure. Compare complete output manifests with in-place emission. Confirm that regeneration neither overwrites user files nor leaves stale generated declarations available after the new translation should have removed them.
specific_remaining_delta: Complete generated-output ownership manifest, user external-model preservation, deletion, and partial failure handling.

section: K. Aeneas translation boundaries and generated output
title: In-memory handoff versus serialized artifacts
requested_scope: Compare file-based LLBC/Lean exchange with available library or structured-stream boundaries. Measure serialization, copying, diagnostics, cancellation, and reproducibility costs. Identify where retaining bytes is valuable evidence and where mandatory files create needless latency or disk growth.
specific_remaining_delta: Measured in-memory/structured-stream versus serialized LLBC/Lean handoff for copying, diagnostics, cancellation, and evidence cost.

section: K. Aeneas translation boundaries and generated output
title: Source correspondence at the selected Aeneas pin
requested_scope: Test the actual metadata available for declaration origins and generated ranges, then compare explicitly selected newer facilities if useful. Determine what Anneal must generate itself for embedded proof edits. Do not assume newer upstream `translation.json` capabilities exist in the selected release.
specific_remaining_delta: Actual Aeneas origin/range metadata at selected pin and explicit adapter mapping needs; newer translation.json requires separate comparison.

section: K. Aeneas translation boundaries and generated output
title: Diagnostics and residual state after translation failure
requested_scope: Exercise rejected inputs, warnings, partial generated files, crashes, and repeated requests. Preserve structured origin where available and test fallback text parsing across pins. Determine whether a failure invalidates only one request or also makes a reusable worker unsafe to retain.
specific_remaining_delta: Warnings, crashes, rejected inputs, partial files, diagnostics origin, and repeated-request residual state across pins.

section: L. Lake preparation and consumer configuration identity

requested_scope: Consume the real prepared Anneal toolchain with empty relevant home/cache state and enforced dependency read-only access. section: L. Lake preparation and consumer configuration identity
title: Consumer package identity matrix
requested_scope: Vary root names, dependency names/indices, graph order, duplicate versions, and absolute/relative paths against one prepared universe. Determine which consumers can reuse package configurations without mutation. Derive the preparation key or supported-shape restriction instead of assuming producer priming covers every workspace.
specific_remaining_delta: Lake package graph order/duplicate/version/rename identity and source/config ablations beyond one package.

section: L. Lake preparation and consumer configuration identity

requested_scope: Change an unsaved projection's import header while keeping the project fixed. Capture `ModuleSetup`, artifacts, plugins, and options used for each query. Test whether global preparation is insufficient and how file-specific readiness should fail when new imports are unavailable.
specific_remaining_delta: Unsaved changed import header with captured per-file ModuleSetup/artifact/plugin/option identity.

section: L. Lake preparation and consumer configuration identity
title: No-build and no-cache as consumer contracts
requested_scope: Exercise missing/stale imports, absent package configs, malformed manifests, and incomplete artifact families under the exact server no-build path. Observe writes, downloads, and exit/status handling. Determine which prerequisites make it a safe read-only consumer and which failures require Anneal-owned preparation.
specific_remaining_delta: No-build/no-cache server path against missing configs, malformed manifest, and all incomplete artifact families.

section: L. Lake preparation and consumer configuration identity
title: Lean versus TOML package configuration
requested_scope: Compare equivalent package declarations with configuration computation, environment dependencies, and dynamic library loading. Identify mutable caches and hidden inputs introduced by executable configuration. Determine whether simplifying generated configuration materially reduces state without restricting necessary user packages.
specific_remaining_delta: TOML versus executable Lean package configuration equivalence, hidden env inputs, and dynamic loading.

section: L. Lake preparation and consumer configuration identity
title: Pinned versus upgraded Lake ownership
requested_scope: Re-run the same consumer-identity and read-only probes at the examined 4.30 pin and explicitly chosen later versions. Account for the rest of the coupled toolchain. Separate a version-specific workaround from a stable architectural requirement; do not infer continuity from nearby release numbers.
specific_remaining_delta: Matched read-only consumer behavior on a deliberately selected later compatible Lean/Lake tuple.

section: L. Lake preparation and consumer configuration identity
title: Observable reuse versus accidental rebuilding
requested_scope: Record launched processes, writes, artifact reads, and setup outputs across repeated checks. Determine reliable reuse indicators even when command output is quiet. Validate actual parallelism controls rather than treating an unrecognized variable such as `LAKE_JOBS` as an enforced resource bound.
specific_remaining_delta: Launched-process, read/write, and trace evidence of actual reuse plus effective parallelism controls.

section: L. Lake preparation and consumer configuration identity
title: Configuration discovery and tool selection
requested_scope: Compare CLI, editor, MCP, CI, and clean-process launches with different working directories, PATH, toolchain selectors, homes, and search paths. Record executable digests and loaded dependencies. Identify which inherited settings must be pinned or rejected to preserve a reproducible prepared environment.
specific_remaining_delta: CLI/editor/MCP/CI launch variants with cwd, PATH, home, selectors, executable digests, and dependencies.

section: M. Cache correctness, packaging, and artifact publication
title: Minimal sufficient cache keys
requested_scope: Perturb each source/model/tool/configuration input while preserving other identities and force lookup through candidate keys. Include source-identical but differently configured runs. Measure false hits and unnecessary misses; a checksum is useful only if it covers the inputs that determine the cached claim.
specific_remaining_delta: Candidate cache-key false-hit/false-miss ablations across source, model, tool, flags, and paths.

section: M. Cache correctness, packaging, and artifact publication
title: Coherent Lean artifact families
requested_scope: Mix, omit, or truncate `.olean` components, `.ilean`, native artifacts, setup metadata, and plugins in isolated fixtures. Test loader rejection, diagnostic quality, and acceptance against a clean control. Establish which artifacts must be published together and which are optional for a specific operation.
specific_remaining_delta: Mixed/truncated cross-generation .olean/.ilean/native/setup/plugin artifact-family controls.

section: M. Cache correctness, packaging, and artifact publication
title: Real clean-versus-prepared equivalence
requested_scope: Compare actual same-platform prepared archives with independently reconstructed environments on representative generated projects. Check declarations, assumptions, relevant artifacts, navigation, and tactic state. Keep byte equality, import success, logical acceptance, and source-level verification as distinct outcomes rather than declaring one universal equivalence oracle.
specific_remaining_delta: Independent clean versus prepared project comparisons of declarations, assumptions, navigation, tactic state, and artifacts.

section: M. Cache correctness, packaging, and artifact publication
title: mtime, trace, and normalization hazards
requested_scope: Change bytes without advancing timestamps, alter source orderings, and exercise old-freshness modes and proposed trace rewrites. Inject changes the comparison must retain. Determine when reuse is unjustified and whether a simpler preparation contract eliminates the need to modify Lake's internal metadata.
specific_remaining_delta: Trace normalization and source-order mutations beyond one same-mtime stale-output control.

section: M. Cache correctness, packaging, and artifact publication
title: Relocation with the producer removed
requested_scope: Move the real environment and generated consumer to different depths, then make the original producer path inaccessible. Test manifests, setup, imports, native libraries, and diagnostics. Compare absolute-path retention with portable packaging; successful use while the old tree still exists is not a relocation test.
specific_remaining_delta: Real generated consumer relocation with original producer inaccessible across setup, native libraries, and diagnostics.

section: M. Cache correctness, packaging, and artifact publication
title: Shared cache publication and interrupted restoration
requested_scope: Use isolated owned caches to race writers/restorers and interrupt downloads, extraction, and publication. Include missing, truncated, and wrong-identity artifacts. Require rejection or recovery without poisoning an already usable environment; distinguish cache-object atomicity from mutations of shared package directories.
specific_remaining_delta: Interrupted concurrent restore/download/extract/publish with wrong-identity and corrupt-object recovery.

section: M. Cache correctness, packaging, and artifact publication
title: Installation identity beyond version labels
requested_scope: Present different permitted local archives under the same nominal version, including an existing installation and interrupted replacement. Record the bytes actually consumed by batch and servers. Determine when installation reuse is legitimate and how mismatches are surfaced without silently comparing an installation to itself.
specific_remaining_delta: Two same-label archives and interrupted install replacement with attested consumed bytes.

section: M. Cache correctness, packaging, and artifact publication
title: Offline and hermetic consumption
requested_scope: Enforce network denial and isolate user caches/configuration while running preparation and proof queries. Trace attempted access, not just command flags. Separate producer downloads from consumer execution and identify environmental dependencies that make a nominally prepared archive incomplete or non-reproducible.
specific_remaining_delta: Enforced network denial and isolated home/cache while tracing attempted access in producer/consumer paths.

section: N. Scheduling, cancellation, crash recovery, and failure states
title: Cancellation through every pipeline stage
requested_scope: Cancel during Cargo/rustc, Charon, Aeneas, Lake setup/build, Lean elaboration, and result publication. Observe descendants, pipes, locks, and temporary outputs. Require bounded cleanup or explicit escalation; successful termination of the parent is not evidence that all work stopped.
specific_remaining_delta: Per-stage real process-group cancellation through Cargo/Charon/Aeneas/Lake/Lean and cleanup.

section: N. Scheduling, cancellation, crash recovery, and failure states
title: Late messages after cancellation
requested_scope: Deliver queued results, diagnostics, progress, and worker exits after cancellation or supersession. Test publication fences and request correlation independently of whether upstream honored cancellation. Preserve cacheable obsolete output only under its original identity and never use silence as a successful result.
specific_remaining_delta: Queued real diagnostics/progress/exit after cancellation with correlation and publication fences.

section: N. Scheduling, cancellation, crash recovery, and failure states
title: Single-flight builds with several consumers
requested_scope: Let multiple proofs request the same dependency generation, then cancel or fail individual consumers. Compare shared in-flight jobs with redundant isolated builds. Test ownership, reference counts, retries, and fan-out of failure so one requester neither corrupts nor indefinitely blocks others.
specific_remaining_delta: Shared actual build with multiple consumers, one cancellation, one failure, and reference-count/fan-out behavior.

section: N. Scheduling, cancellation, crash recovery, and failure states
title: Lock ordering and publication deadlocks
requested_scope: Combine environment preparation, generation publication, cache insertion, worker restart, and garbage collection. Inject pauses after lock acquisition and crashes while waiting. Identify ordering cycles and unbounded waits; compare coarse locks with a simpler ownership model before adding fine-grained coordination.
specific_remaining_delta: Real lock ordering across prepare/publish/cache/restart/GC with injected pauses and bounded waits.

section: N. Scheduling, cancellation, crash recovery, and failure states
title: Timeouts and resource exhaustion
requested_scope: Use bounded fixtures that exhaust time, memory, disk, file descriptors, or process slots. Distinguish proof failure from incomplete checking and infrastructure failure. Verify cleanup and recovery while preserving the previous usable generation; do not let empty diagnostics after termination imply success.
specific_remaining_delta: Bounded time, memory, disk, descriptor, and process-slot exhaustion with recovery and last-good preservation.

section: N. Scheduling, cancellation, crash recovery, and failure states
title: Restart reconstruction under forced failures
requested_scope: Kill the worker, watchdog, Anneal process, and build subprocess separately at recorded states. Reconstruct from authoritative inputs without inherited memory. Compare results to fresh checks and distinguish a restartable partial workspace from a generation whose publication never completed.
specific_remaining_delta: Forced worker/watchdog/Anneal/build-process kills and reconstruction from authoritative inputs.

section: N. Scheduling, cancellation, crash recovery, and failure states
title: Interactive fairness and edit storms
requested_scope: Combine expensive batch checks with rapid proof edits, many agents, and a slow document. Compare debouncing, prioritization, bounded queues, and cancellation strategies. Measure tail latency, useful completed work, and starvation; latest-only correctness must not make the interface permanently unresponsive.
specific_remaining_delta: Measured tail latency/starvation under edit storms, slow documents, multiple agents, and batch load.

section: N. Scheduling, cancellation, crash recovery, and failure states
title: Lost filesystem and transport events
requested_scope: Drop, duplicate, and reorder watcher notifications and disconnect transports while work proceeds. Compare event-only invalidation with explicit state reconciliation. Determine how the system detects missed changes and restores freshness without requiring every watcher or client connection to deliver events exactly once.
specific_remaining_delta: Dropped/duplicated/reordered real watcher and transport events with explicit state reconciliation.

section: O. Disk amplification, memory, throughput, and latency
title: Per-consumer disk bill of materials
requested_scope: Attribute logical bytes, allocated blocks, inode counts, bytes written, and peak temporary space to Rust products, LLBC, generated Lean, local `.lake` state, dependencies, caches, and logs. Measure correctness, throughput, tail latency, CPU, memory, and disk before further increases. Test the intended high-worker workload without assuming that two successful consumers extrapolate or deliberately exhausting an uncontrolled host.

requested_scope: Sweep outer job count and supported inner controls for Cargo/rustc, Aeneas, Lake, and Lean. Observe real threads/processes and peak resource use. Determine where one global budget can be enforced and where independently reasonable defaults cause oversubscription or misleading benchmarks.

title: Sustained edit/query soak
requested_scope: Run long sessions with proof edits, model changes, opened/closed files, scratch attempts, and worker restarts. Track retained environments, generations, handles, and processes. requested_scope: Measure capture, projection, extraction, translation, import preparation, elaboration, and query response separately. Compare proof-only, Rust-model, import-header, and toolchain changes at several realistic sizes. Identify whether startup, serialization, generation churn, or actual proof work dominates before choosing an optimization.
specific_remaining_delta: Stage-by-stage end-to-end latency under proof-only, model, import, and toolchain changes at realistic sizes.

requested_scope: Compare direct read-only consumption, symlinks, hardlinks, reflinks, and copies on relevant filesystems. Attempt expected consumer writes in owned fixtures and inspect the producer. section: O. Disk amplification, memory, throughput, and latency

requested_scope: Extend proofs with new imports, tactics, macros, plugins, and scratch documents after preparing a pruned dependency universe. requested_scope: Retire generations while workers, pending queries, scratch forks, and replay records still reference them. Test imported memory maps and later file opens, not just open handles. title: Workspace trust and code execution boundary
requested_scope: Inventory execution by build scripts, proc macros, Lake configuration, Lean commands/tactics, and native extensions.
