title: Fault-injection state-machine harness
requested_scope: Model the engine with controllable fake stages and enumerate bounded schedules of edits, publications, failures, cancellation, and restarts. Check explicit invariants and save minimal counterexamples. Replay selected schedules against real tools; a passing model alone does not establish implementation conformance.
specific_remaining_delta: Broader model schedules plus replay against a real engine rather than only a fake subprocess adapter.

section: Q. Acceptance, oracles, and adversarial test methodology
title: Real concurrency transcripts with causal barriers
requested_scope: Use controllable handshakes or instrumentation to place edits and rebuilds inside actual in-flight requests. Preserve ordering evidence and request/worker identities. Separate deterministic sequential demonstrations from genuine races, then repeat and minimize failures rather than relying only on nondeterministic sleeps.
specific_remaining_delta: Actual in-flight edit/rebuild causal barriers and worker/request identities across stages.

section: Q. Acceptance, oracles, and adversarial test methodology
title: Interaction matrix and negative controls
requested_scope: Cover pairwise combinations of source changes, import changes, cache states, launch modes, and lifecycle events, adding higher-order cases suggested by failures. Seed stale outputs, missing obligations, wrong subjects, and changed assumptions. Verify the harness detects them before trusting green runs.
specific_remaining_delta: Pairwise/higher-order source/import/cache/launch/lifecycle matrix and seeded wrong-subject/assumption controls.

section: Q. Acceptance, oracles, and adversarial test methodology
title: Independent reproduction and cross-version boundaries
requested_scope: Reproduce the highest-consequence findings with an independent environment/operator and exact pins, then compare deliberately selected compatible toolchain upgrades. Classify fixes, regressions, unsupported tuples, and untested cells separately. Preserve old findings about old subjects rather than marking them obsolete because a new version differs.
specific_remaining_delta: Independent operator/environment reproduction and selected compatible toolchain upgrade matrix.

section: R. Integrated prototypes, usability, and staged decisions
title: Minimal embedded-proof vertical slice
requested_scope: Build one disposable prototype that opens an unsaved Lean annotation, projects it, queries goals, applies a version-checked edit, and checks the captured result in batch. Use a prepared generated model and retain all context identities. This tests the scaffolding seam without requiring interactive Charon or Aeneas.
specific_remaining_delta: Real Rust-hosted annotation with parser, projection, prepared model, exact live query/edit, and batch check.

section: R. Integrated prototypes, usability, and staged decisions
title: Full model-change vertical slice
requested_scope: Extend the prototype with a Rust edit that changes the generated model, including a failing intermediate generation and a late obsolete result. Query before/during/after publication and compare fresh checks. Require explicit old/new/provisional states and no accidental mixture of source or imports.
specific_remaining_delta: Real Charon/Aeneas model-change sequence with pending/failing/late generations and before/during/after queries.

section: R. Integrated prototypes, usability, and staged decisions
title: Real parallel-test acceptance scenario
requested_scope: Run isolated generated projects against the actual shared read-only toolchain, with model edits, scratch trials, forced restarts, and cleanup. Combine the disk inventory and concurrency sweep. Define acceptable bounds from measurements and host budgets, not a promise of zero overhead or a fixed universal worker count.
specific_remaining_delta: Actual parallel Anneal generated-project tests combining edit/scratch/restart/cleanup and resource bounds.

section: R. Integrated prototypes, usability, and staged decisions
title: Agent proof-edit correctness and maintenance
requested_scope: Give controlled authoring and repair tasks with known contracts and allowed assumptions. Compare exact goal/context access with simpler batch feedback under matched budgets. Score intended-statement preservation, stale-query errors, conflicts, intervention, and resource use—not just accepted Lean or tool-call count.
specific_remaining_delta: Multiple controlled agent tasks with counterbalanced feedback order, matched cognitive budgets, and broader contracts.

section: R. Integrated prototypes, usability, and staged decisions
title: Human understanding of freshness and failure
requested_scope: Evaluate presentation of stale models, pending imports, cancelled work, unsupported translation, approximate locations, and expired goal handles. Test whether readers choose the intended subject and a sound repair. Improve the interface without weakening result semantics or forcing ordinary Rust users into generated Lean internals.
specific_remaining_delta: Human participants and interface comprehension trials for stale/pending/cancelled/unsupported/approximate states.

section: R. Integrated prototypes, usability, and staged decisions
title: Measured adoption gates for optional optimizations
requested_scope: Use prior results to compare subprocess reuse, finer-grained invalidation, incremental projection, shared brokers, and historical snapshot retention with their simpler baselines. Record benefits, added invariants, and failure cases. Reject or defer optimizations whose complexity is not justified by measured workloads.
specific_remaining_delta: Measured optional-optimization gates against simple baselines and documented invariant/failure costs.

section: R. Integrated prototypes, usability, and staged decisions
title: Remote and durable execution, only if needed
requested_scope: Test a small versioned proof job across an isolated remote/local boundary, including retries, authentication, cancellation, artifact identity, and result validation. Determine which local contracts already suffice. Do not introduce distributed orchestration or persistent sessions unless an actual workflow justifies them.
specific_remaining_delta: Conditionally justified remote/local proof job with authenticated retry/cancel/artifact identity, if local limits require it.

section: R. Integrated prototypes, usability, and staged decisions
title: Decision and regression synthesis
requested_scope: For each tested hypothesis, record supporting evidence, counterexamples, untested stronger claims, chosen fallback, and the smallest regression probe. Identify the v2 interfaces that must change now versus later options. Keep factual reports in `reference` and adopted design in its proper authority; this synthesis must not silently adopt every prototype.
specific_remaining_delta: Decision synthesis after remaining experiments: evidence, counterexample, fallback, regression, and v2 interface choice.

section: Scope extensions
title: Minimum cross-layer identity by ablation
requested_scope: Prototype an identity tuple containing Cargo subject, exact source snapshot, Charon tool/configuration, LLBC digest, Aeneas tool/configuration, generated-tree digest, prepared Lake environment, import traces/hashes, projected URI/version/hash, server generation, file-worker incarnation, and RPC-session incarnation. Remove one dimension at a time and seek a counterexample. Keep locators constant while changing payloads at every stage; compare A→B→A, byte-identical output from different upstream histories, semantically equivalent but byte-different output, and unchanged proof text with changed imports. Distinguish monotonic causality from reusable content identity. Test a thin-adapter response envelope carrying workspace/generation, source/projected positions, current/stale status, actual environment, goal/diagnostic payload, and separately optional verification status.
specific_remaining_delta: Full cross-layer identity ablation including Cargo, Charon, Aeneas, LLBC, Lake, import trace, URI/version/worker/RPC.

section: Scope extensions
title: Retention versus recomputation economics
requested_scope: Compare retaining source only; source plus projection; generated Lean; workspace-local Lake state; compiled generated modules; and live workers. Sweep 1/2/4/8/16 retained generations within host budgets. Measure disk, memory, reconstruction latency, and correctness of historical goals against old imports. Compare retained worker, reconstructed projection, fresh worker over retained artifacts, and refusal. Determine when a revision handle should expire rather than implying durable historical-query support.
specific_remaining_delta: Retention tiers on actual generated outputs with memory, historical-goal latency, recomputation, and restart costs.

section: Scope extensions
title: Source/artifact changes decoupled from each other
requested_scope: Replace an imported `.olean` while leaving source unchanged, varying relevant timestamps; separately change source but obtain byte-identical rebuilt semantic artifacts. Include changed external models with unchanged Aeneas output. Query existing and refreshed workers and compare fresh batch controls. Determine when artifact identity forces reload, when restart is merely conservative, and which additional options/native/setup identities prevent byte equality from establishing an equivalent environment.
specific_remaining_delta: Source unchanged/artifact changed and source changed/semantic artifact same with both old and fresh workers.

section: Scope extensions
title: Translation determinism and harmless textual instability
requested_scope: Repeat identical Charon extractions and Aeneas generations sequentially and concurrently at Anneal's intended flags, split-file layout, and parallel settings. Preserve raw LLBC and Lean and separately compare justified semantic relationships. Investigate ordering/comment/formatting changes that leave the intended model equivalent but invalidate raw hashes, Lake traces, or Lean command-prefix reuse. Measure downstream cost before normalizing keys; retain source/provenance differences that matter to editing or evidence.
specific_remaining_delta: Determinism across sequential/concurrent Charon/Aeneas modes, flags, split layout, and semantic comparator.

section: Scope extensions
title: Cross-layer declaration and generation manifest
requested_scope: Prototype one machine-readable handoff manifest with subject/tool/configuration identities, source LLBC digest, complete generated file list, module/import graph, declaration identities, and coarse source provenance. Relate compiler-resolved Rust items through Charon declarations and Aeneas pure declarations to generated Lean declarations and Anneal obligations, including one-to-many helpers. Keep exact editable proof ranges separate. Test navigation, deletion, and invalidation consumers; establish what Anneal must supply at its selected Aeneas pin without assuming newer `translation.json` support.
specific_remaining_delta: Machine-readable manifest with exact cross-layer identities, complete file/module/declaration graph, and proven mappings.

section: Scope extensions
title: Prepared-environment contract by operation
requested_scope: Enumerate required inputs/artifacts/configuration for batch build, `lake env lean --json`, `lake serve`, per-file `setup-file`, InfoView/RPC, and native plugin/dynamic-library use. Classify producer-owned immutable state, consumer-owned mutable state, and any explicitly permitted shared-writable cache. Test the minimum source/control-plane material plus artifact cache as a reconstruction candidate and identify missing classes. Derive the identity under which pooling is valid rather than using a single unqualified “prepared” flag.
specific_remaining_delta: All operation-specific prepared inputs for lake serve, setup-file, InfoView/RPC, native/plugin use, and ownership.

section: Scope extensions
title: Shared writable build-tree counterexample study
requested_scope: In owned disposable fixtures, compare consumers sharing one writable package directory or generated-module build directory with isolated consumers over a frozen producer. Run identical and conflicting builds and interrupt writers at controlled publication points. Check cache maps, partial outputs, subsequent reads/retries, and cross-consumer definitions. Seek the strongest valid shared-writer contract or preserve a minimal failure—not a preselected negative result. Keep artifact-cache publication distinct from shared package-directory mutation.
specific_remaining_delta: Conflicting simultaneous writes and controlled kill at output/trace publication with cache inspection.

section: Scope extensions
title: MCP subscriptions versus polling
requested_scope: On explicitly supported protocol revisions, prototype subscriptions/change streams for generation changes, diagnostics, proof readiness, and verification completion; compare polling and explicit state reconciliation. Drop or delay notifications, disconnect clients, and retry result retrieval. Determine whether subscriptions improve responsiveness while polling/reconciliation remains the correctness path, and provide a capability fallback rather than presuming every MCP client supports the same mechanism.
specific_remaining_delta: Executable MCP subscription versus polling under dropped/delayed messages and state reconciliation.

section: Scope extensions
title: Server, MCP, and scratch-pool topology
requested_scope: For one prepared environment, compare N open proof files under one watchdog with N independent servers. Compare one MCP process serving many sessions, environments, or repositories with per-workspace adapters and an external broker. Sweep 1/2/4/8/... prewarmed scratch documents and compare fresh scratch creation, prefix reuse, teardown, memory, latency, and process ownership. Use conflicting definitions/options/plugins to detect cross-workspace reuse; do not pool independently configured projects merely because document APIs accept their URIs.
specific_remaining_delta: Matched one-watchdog versus N-server and MCP broker/adapters with 1/2/4/8 docs and scratch churn.

section: Scope extensions
title: Fixture sharing and contamination sentinels
requested_scope: Compare one workspace per test, one per fixture with multiple phases, and one per logical suite. Give each test a unique model definition or option that makes accidental reuse observable; include conflicting plugins where supported. Run phases in different orders and parallel schedules, interrupt selected workers, then rerun subsequent tests. Measure disk/setup savings against required reset/isolation guarantees rather than replacing heavyweight sandboxes with untested shared mutable state.
specific_remaining_delta: Per-test/per-fixture/per-suite contamination controls including plugins, phase ordering, and worker restarts.

section: Scope extensions
title: Shadow files and hidden Lean-document lifecycle
requested_scope: If Lean/Lake requires physical paths, distinguish internal file-backed URIs from editor-facing logical documents. Independently of backing choice, open/change/save/rename/close a Rust host and trace hidden document creation, workers, updates, and cleanup. Keep unsaved source authoritative while deliberately stale or missing shadow files exist; crash/restart and reconstruct without treating mirrors as canonical. Test whether custom URIs require shadow paths, and whether model regeneration can preserve authored proof identity while changing the environment generation.
specific_remaining_delta: Rust-host open/change/save/rename/close through hidden Lean document lifecycle and cleanup.

section: Scope extensions
title: Explicit backend capability negotiation
requested_scope: Prototype versioned descriptors for accepting unsaved inputs, filesystem materialization requirements, concurrent requests, cancellation, deterministic output, persistent process support, and fine-grained invalidation. Test descriptors against actual implementations and unsupported combinations. Distinguish a documented promise from measured behavior; choose conservative fallback or explicit failure when capabilities are absent rather than letting a uniform logical API imply uniform implementation guarantees.
specific_remaining_delta: Versioned tested backend capability descriptors, fallback, and unsupported-call behavior.

section: Scope extensions
title: Batch and transport-free live shells over one engine
requested_scope: Build a small batch shell and an in-process repeated edit/query driver over the same structured engine. Compare the batch shell with current CLI behavior where implemented and the live driver with fresh checks on identical captured inputs. Include model changes, cancellation, and reconstruction before adding an LSP/MCP transport. Identify divergence caused by the engine separately from adapter protocol bugs; the prototype does not claim the current CLI already implements every stage.
specific_remaining_delta: One shared engine exercised by batch and in-process repeated live driver against current CLI/fresh oracle.

section: Scope extensions
title: Minimal interactive upgrade suite and workaround deletion probes
requested_scope: Derive a small retained replay suite for compatible toolchain tuples. For Lean/Lake, cover configuration ownership, workspace isolation, dependency refresh, goal versioning, server setup, and artifact families. For Charon, cover LLBC schema, span units, process lifecycle, determinism, and subject identity. For Aeneas, cover mutable globals, package layout, naming, provenance, determinism, and library/incremental APIs. Associate every manifest/trace/mtime/rewrite workaround with the exact behavior requiring it and a probe that would justify removal. Compare the examined 4.30 pin with 4.31 or another explicitly selected compatible candidate; retain accurate old-version findings and do not create a competing mutable corpus lifecycle.
specific_remaining_delta: Retained cross-tool replay suite on selected compatible upgrades with workaround deletion probes.

section: Scope extensions
title: Deliberately challenge the proposed architecture
requested_scope: Run the following as falsification controls in the relevant existing harnesses, not twelve duplicate surveys. Build the strongest plausible simple alternative; record the smallest counterexample or exact successful preconditions. Do not assume the leading design must win.
specific_remaining_delta: Twelve falsification controls executed in relevant real harnesses, with strongest simple alternatives and exact preconditions.
